p: a king shall reign in righteousness: This prophecy is of Hezekiah, who was a figure of Christ, and therefore it should chiefly be referred to him.
rule in judgment: By judgment and justice is meant an upright government, both in policy and religion.
a weary land: Where men are weary with travelling for lack of water.

them that see shall not be: He promises to give the true light which is the pure doctrine of God's word, and understanding, and zeal of the same, are contrary to the threatenings against the wicked, Isa 6:9,29:10.
vile person shall be no more: Vice will no more be called virtue, nor virtue esteemed by power and riches.
careless daughters: He prophecies of such calamity to come that they will not spare the women and children, and therefore wills them to take heed and provide.
ye careless women: Meaning that the affliction would continue long and when one year was past, yet they should look for new plagues.
for the vintage shall fail: God will take from you the means and opportunities, which made you contemn him: that is, abundance of worldly goods.
breasts: By the breasts he means the plentiful fields, by which men are nourished as children with the breast: or, the mothers for sorrow and heaviness will lack milk.

spirit shall be poured upon us: That is, when the Church will be restored, thus the prophets after they have denounced God's judgments against the wicked, used to comfort the godly, lest they should faint.

fruitful field shall be counted for: The field which is now fruitful, will be but as a barren forest in comparison to what it will be then as in Isa 29:17 which will be fulfilled in Christ's time, for then they who were before as the barren wilderness, being regenerate will be fruitful and they who had some beginning of godliness, will bring forth fruit in such abundance, that their former life will seem but as a wilderness where no fruit was.
city shall be low in a: They will not need to build it in high places for fear of the enemy: for God will defend it, and turn away the storms from hurting their conveniences.
that sow beside all waters: That is, upon fat ground and well watered, which brings forth in abundance, or in places which before were covered with waters, and now made dry for your uses.
send forth there the feet of: The fields will be so rank, that they will send out their cattle to eat up the first crop, which abundance will be signs of God's love and favour toward them.
